title: Coherent adic systems on algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Modules and their ordinary sheaf kernels and cokernels are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; quasi-coherence, tensor pullback and direct image are on these ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Locally Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means additionally quasi-compact and quasi-separated, where quasi-compact means every open covering has a finite subcover and quasi-separated means the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent].

For a Noetherian $X$ and a quasi-coherent ideal $J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-sfb-space-quasi-coherent-ideal], define $\mathrm{Coh}(X,J)$ to have objects inverse systems $(M_n,t_n)_{n\geq1}$ of coherent modules, with $t_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$, with $J^nM_n=0$, and with $t_n$ inducing an isomorphism $M_{n+1}/J^nM_{n+1}\simeq M_n$. An arrow $a:(M_n,t_n)\to(N_n,s_n)$ is a family $a_n:M_n\to N_n$ with $a_n t_n=s_n a_{n+1}$; identities and composition are componentwise. Here $J^0M=M$ and $J^nM$ for $n\geq1$ is the submodule locally generated by products of $n$ ideal sections and one module section; $M/J^nM$ is its ordinary sheaf cokernel. For a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $M$, define its completion diagram $\widehat M_J=(M/J^nM)_{n\geq1}$ with quotient transitions, and send a module map to its induced maps on these quotients. For a morphism $g:X\to Y$ and a system $(N_n,s_n)$ on $Y$, write $g^*(N_n)$ for the diagram with terms $g^*N_n$ and transitions $g^*s_n$.

When $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is separated of finite type [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties, def-weil-affine-spectrum], where $A$ is a commutative ring, a system has proper support when $M_1$ admits a proper closed carrier over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in the sense of [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. This means $M_1\simeq i_*Q$ for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ proper and $Q$ finite type quasi-coherent. For a morphism $a:(M_n)\to(N_n)$ and another quasi-coherent ideal $K$, say its kernel and cokernel are killed by a power of $K$ when some integer $t\geq1$ kills every ordinary sheaf kernel and cokernel of $a_n$, for all $n\geq1$. This bounded condition refers to the component maps, not to termwise computation of kernels in the category of adic systems.

lean.note: Positive levels use op n for level n+1. Coherence is site quasi-coherence and the existing RingedSpace.IsCoherent on each schemeRestriction. Quotient data are selected only from the full projection-normalized cokernel universal property and its unique natural-isomorphism characterization. Completion is supplied both as the quotient-diagram functor and as a functor from coherent modules into Coh(X,J). Proper support uses a finite-type quasi-coherent module on a closed proper carrier. Uniform annihilation quantifies over ordinary ambient kernel and cokernel universal properties, not over kernels in the adic category. The three added statement dependencies already have landed records. Section 1(B), Q72 returned-delivery repair: retain the live module, primary declaration, signature and all 14 declarations, and append the three general-base support definitions in the owning module. The original Spec A support interface cannot accept the consumer's arbitrary S-base. The added predicates retain exactly the same closed proper carrier and the existing chart-coherence predicate, with no extra mathematical assumptions.
